newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares to be in choppy range ahead of Fed.
newsitem.headline: German shares to be in choppy range ahead of Fed.

text.p: German shares will likely remain under modest selling pressure ahead of Tuesday's crucial Federal Reserve board meeting amid speculation that U.S. interest rates will be nudged slightly higher.

The 30-share DAX index, which ended bourse trade on Monday down 19.06 points at 2,627.04, will not likely dip below 2,620 points ahead of the meeting but will not test the record high set last Friday at 2,647.78 points.
"After all the excitement on Friday, the market today is rather dead," said one Frankfurt trader, noting he did not expect much movement before Tuesday's Fed meeting.
The German market, according to some traders, has factored in the Fed raising short-term rates by about 25 basis points.
"People are holding off ahead of the Fed and are generally unwilling to buy at these levels," said one trader.
German broker Trinkaus & Burkhardt said a modest U.S. rate hike would still allow German shares to keep up the record advance and to reach the 2,700 level by early 1997.

Among specific shares on Monday, dollar-sensitive chemical shares were unable to buck the downward trend despite a firm dollar, with Hoechst AG falling 34 pfennigs to 54.91 marks and BASF down 60 pfennigs at 47.18 marks.
Insurance group Munich Re held up fairly well on its DAX 30 debut given the market conditions, falling just three marks to 3,447.00 marks.
Linotype-Hell AG ended up seven marks at 130 marks after the company said its chief executive would quit. He will be replaced by an executive from Linotype's new owner, Heidelberger Druck.
